blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.’s commitment to hold police accountable for past and ongoing abuses in the government’s anti-drug campaign has fallen short, Human Rights Watch (HRW) said. The statement came ahead of the Nov. 30 trial of former President Rodrigo Duterte at the International Criminal Court (ICC), with HRW saying the government needs to prioritize justice for all victims and provide their families with adequate redress. HRW recalled that in 2022, Marcos pledged to pursue prosecutions over killings in the previous administration’s war on drugs and established a task force for that purpose.
